title: Quantifying Medical Histories with the Kaplan-Meier Estimator for Feature Extraction
author: Herdiantri Sufriyana
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.21203/rs.3.pex-1635/v2
materials: Supp_protocol_hist_rate.Pdf Supplementary information for source code description

steps.title: Quantify medical histories into time intervals
steps.instruction: Compute the number of days for a specific code or variable in the latest encounter occurring before the current visit (d 0).

substeps.instruction: Use variables that assign multiple codes of diagnosis and procedure.

steps.title: Infer population-level KM estimates
steps.instruction: Use the derivation set to infer Kaplan-Meier (KM) estimates as an estimator of the historical function H(d), representing the probability or fraction of visits where a condition lasts longer than d days before d 0.

substeps.instruction: Identify d i as the day when at least one encounter occurred for a code or variable referring to the condition.
Identify e i as the number of encounters for the code or variable on day d i.
Identify v i as a visit recorded that did not encounter the code or variable (censored) up to day d i.

steps.title: Interpolate missing KM estimate time points
steps.instruction: Apply linear interpolation between time points where a KM estimate could not be calculated due to days with no encountered codes or variables in the population.

steps.title: Transform individual medical histories into rates
steps.instruction: Convert the number of days from a code or variable encounter to the current visit for an individual into a historical rate by matching it with the nationwide historical (KM) rates derived from the training set.
